claims.claim: ROOT CAUSE of the earlier 0-mesh result: MeshTrackingManager requires subscribeAnchorUpdate BEFORE start(). PICO's Spatial Mesh doc states it plainly — 'You need to subscribe to the mesh anchor's AnchorUpdate event before the start function can push update data.' The first probe called start() with no subscription and got 0. With the subscription first, 42 anchors arrived after roughly 7 seconds.

MEASURED COORDINATE FACTS for plane hit-testing, recorded so nobody re-derives them. PlaneAnchor.vertices are LOCAL to the anchor, not world. A plane's local quad lies in the XZ plane (every vertex has y == 0), so the plane NORMAL is local +Y — NOT forward. An earlier version of this hit test used FORWARD and consequently reported a horizontal ray hitting the FLOOR, which was a real bug. Observed vertices sit at exactly +/-boundingBoxSize, so that field behaves as a HALF-extent here; deriving bounds from the vertices avoids depending on that.

CAVEAT for anyone building on this: WALL planes are small SEGMENTS, not whole wall surfaces — observed sizes include 1.687 x 0.847, 0.825 x 0.214 and 1.189 x 0.124 m, with 15 WALL planes in the room. A blind horizontal ray sweep at fixed eye height hit nothing across all 12 compass bearings, purely because rays passed between segments. Do not conclude from a missed ray that hit-testing is broken; aim at geometry or use the meshes.
